title: Your Phone Screen Can't Feel a Glove
fb_caption: Put on winter gloves and your phone stops listening. Under the glass sits an invisible grid of tiny electrodes holding a small electric field. Your fingertip conducts electricity, so it changes the charge where you touch, and the phone pinpoints the spot. A regular glove is an insulator, so it blocks that change and the screen feels nothing. Touchscreen gloves weave conductive thread into the fingertip, so it acts like bare skin. Do you take your gloves off, or own a touchscreen pair?
engagement_comment: Do you take your gloves off, or own a touchscreen pair? 1 = gloves off every time, 2 = touchscreen gloves, 3 = I just wait until I'm inside.
sources: Wikipedia, Touchscreen (capacitive: grid of crossing conductors; a finger disturbs the electric field and changes the capacitance, which the controller detects; some capacitive screens cannot detect a finger through insulating material such as gloves): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchscreen

Nelson Miller, Why Can't I Wear Gloves With My Touchscreen? (a bare finger draws off some of the screen's charge and the change in capacitance is read as a touch; gloves restrict that flow): https://nelson-miller.com/why-cant-i-wear-gloves-with-my-touchscreen

Gear Patrol, The Science Behind Touchscreen Gloves (conductive material, most often copper yarn, woven into the fingertip acts as a bare finger): https://www.gearpatrol.com/outdoors/smartphone-compatible-gloves-explained/
